rows.reason: Key size is a fixed parameter; the FIPS 197 App. B/C.1 (C.3 for the AES-256 stretch) known-answer vectors give a pass/fail verdict, not a distribution.
Encrypt and decrypt directions are checked against fixed FIPS 197 vectors in both directions; the verdict is deterministic.
Datapath equivalence is a deterministic testbench comparison against the golden model for every vector, plus STA at the named corners; no random sampling.
ECB-only scope is checked against the fixed SP 800-38A F.1 ECB vectors; the verdict is exact match or mismatch.
Key-schedule correctness is a KAT; round keys never reaching the bus is a formal property proven over all paths, which is a proof, not a sampled estimate.
Latency is an exact cycle count from the testbench; the 220 ns figure is that count times the 20 ns period and is unmeasured on silicon.
SHA-256 core is checked against fixed FIPS 180-4 vectors (abc, 448-bit, million-a); exact digest match.
Message-length limit is a 32-bit counter width; the testbench exercises named boundary lengths 55, 56, 63, 64 and 119 with exact expected digests.
Padding is checked by KATs at the padding boundary lengths; the verdict is exact digest match.
HMAC-SHA-256 is checked against RFC 4231 cases 1-4, 6 and 7; exact tag match.
Key handling is stated as formal properties P-3 and P-5, proven over all paths on RTL and the synthesized netlist; a proof outcome, not a statistic.
Latency is an exact testbench cycle count; the 1.3 us figure is that count times the clock period, with STA at the named corner as the timing verdict.
Root key input handling is a testbench check plus formal property P-1 over all paths; no distribution is involved.
KDF is checked against published SP 800-108 counter-mode vectors where available, else a golden-model cross-check; exact output match.
Slot count is a fixed design parameter; testbench behavior plus formal property P-2 give a deterministic verdict.
Slot permissions are a per-slot mask checked by testbench and formal properties P-5; deterministic proof outcome.
Lock-bit behavior is stated as formal property P-6, proven over all paths; a proof outcome, not a sampled estimate.
Slot visibility is stated as formal properties P-1 and P-2, proven over all paths; there is no sampled or probabilistic evidence.
CTR_DRBG construction is checked against the SP 800-90A AES-128 with derivation-function example vectors; exact output match. No entropy quantity is measured.
Seed handling is a deterministic testbench comparison against the golden model for a fixed seed input; the word counts are design parameters.
Reseed handling is a deterministic testbench comparison against the golden model for a fixed input; the word count is a design parameter.
Reseed interval and request size are fixed counter limits, checked by testbench and formal property P-8; a deterministic proof outcome.
Stall and zeroize behavior on gated and alarm is a control-path property: formal P-9 for alarm, testbench for the gated stall; no statistical quantity.
No output before seeding is formal property P-7, proven over all paths; a proof outcome.

This row states a claim wording and claims no entropy figure; entropy stays provisional until silicon and is the sibling TRNG's. Nothing here is measured, so no statistical evidence exists or is required.
Reset zeroization is formal property P-10, proven over all paths; a proof outcome.
Alarm zeroization of every key slot is formal property P-9, proven over all paths; a proof outcome.
Bus-violation handling is a testbench check plus formal property P-11; deterministic proof outcome.
The gated stall transition is a deterministic testbench check of state-machine behavior; no statistical quantity.
Software ZEROIZE is a deterministic testbench check of the resulting state and register contents, with P-10 covering the zeroized state.
Bus protocol conformance is a deterministic testbench protocol-checker verdict.
Bus width is a fixed design parameter confirmed by testbench; exact pass/fail.
Status register and irq behavior are checked by deterministic testbench assertions.
No register returning key, seed or DRBG state is formal properties P-1 through P-4, proven over all paths; a proof outcome.
Clock closure is a static timing verdict per liberty corner: setup at ss_100C_1v60, hold at ff_n40C_1v95, and all other sky130_fd_sc_hd corners via klt sta. Corner-bounded, not a distribution.
AES block latency is an exact testbench cycle count, with STA at the named corner ss_100C_1v60 as the timing verdict.
SHA-256 block latency is an exact testbench cycle count, with STA at the named corner ss_100C_1v60 as the timing verdict.
Area is a single synthesized cell-area figure at corner tt_025C_1v80 from the SYNTH and P&R reports; a point value against a placeholder budget, not a distribution.
Signoff is the klt drc and klt lvs verdicts, each clean or not; deterministic.
